h1:
Koh Samui Nightlife Plan
Chaweng, Beach Clubs & Bars
intro: Samui nights come in different moods, from sipping cocktails on soft cushions by the water watching a fire show, to dancing barefoot on the sand and big clubs that run until sunrise. We've laid it out as a 3-night plan that builds from chill to lively, so you can pick whichever night fits your mood, with real drink prices and how to get back to your hotel safely.

blocks.html: First, a quick lay of the land. Samui nightlife splits into three main areas. Bophut – Fisherman's Village is the chill one: sit back, sip something, watch a fire show, soak up the old-town vibe · Chaweng Beach is the centre of the fun, with beach clubs that party from afternoon into the night, the big clubs, and a strip of bars · while Lamai Beach is more low-key than Chaweng, a slightly older crowd, live reggae and classic rock. This three-night plan covers all three.

blocks.text: Night 1 — Bophut Fisherman's Village, chill by the sea

blocks.html: Keep the first night easy. Start at Bophut Fisherman's Village, the row of old Chinese shophouses on the north coast of the island. Wander, snack, sip a cocktail, then finish at a beach bar watching a fire show. It's a good night for couples or for anyone who just landed and is a bit worn out.

items.activity: Stroll Bophut Fisherman's Village, find dinner
items.note: If you come on a Friday, the street closes into a Walking Street with food and live music, roughly 17:00–23:00

items.activity: Find a seafood spot or a seaside restaurant in the area
items.note: Prices in this tourist area run higher than at general markets, so check the menu before you order

items.activity: Head to CoCo Tam's, a Bophut beach bar, and grab a sandbag cushion for the fire-spinning show
items.note: Fire shows happen most nights, cocktails start around ฿250–350. Drinks here are bar prices, not convenience-store prices
Call a taxi or motorbike taxi through an app, or always agree on the price before you get on

blocks.title: Pick your seat early
blocks.html: At beach bars like CoCo Tam's, the sand-side cushion seats fill up fast from sunset into the early evening. If you want a clear view of the fire show, grab a seat before 19:00 and you'll have an easier time.

blocks.text: Night 2 — Chaweng Beach, beach clubs and dancing on the sand

blocks.html: Tonight you move to Chaweng Beach, the heart of the island's fun. Start at a beach club in the evening, sit by the water with a DJ playing, then drift into the bar zone. If you fancy something a bit fancier, there's Woo Bar at W Samui with seats sunk into a reflecting pool over the sea view, though prices match the hotel's level.

items.name: Ark Bar Beach Club
items.blurb: The Chaweng regular. There's a pool party on the sand every day from around 2pm, with DJs and fire shows, and it gets packed at night. Good for anyone who wants to dance barefoot on the beach.
items.meta: Central Chaweng · open from morning until 2am

items.name: CoCo Tam's
items.blurb: The real chill spot, over in Bophut. Sandbag cushions by the water, swing seats at the bar, fire-spinning most nights. Better for settling in and talking than for dancing.

items.name: Woo Bar (W Koh Samui)
items.blurb: A luxury hotel bar with seats sunk into a reflecting pool facing the sea, signature cocktails, prices to match the level. Good for photos and a nice atmosphere to sip in.

items.name: SEEN Beach Club
items.blurb: A stylish beach club with DJ sets, a pool and seating by the water, and a slightly more dressed-up crowd. Good if you want an upscale feel but still room to dance.

items.name: The Deck
items.blurb: A seaside cocktail bar with a chiller tone than the party beach clubs, easy DJ sets. Good for a drink before or after you head out dancing somewhere else.

items.activity: Head into a beach club on Chaweng (like Ark Bar or SEEN) and grab a spot for sunset
items.note: Some places have a cover charge or minimum spend on event days, so check their page before you go

items.activity: Have a light dinner around Chaweng to fuel up for a long night
items.note: Lining your stomach before drinking helps you last longer and keep yourself in check

items.activity: Back to the beach club when the DJ comes on, dance on the sand, catch the fire show
items.note: Drinks in the club run 2–3x convenience-store prices, so set a budget in your head

items.activity: Head home or carry on to the club zone (see Night 3)
items.note: Don't leave your glass and walk off. Always keep drinking from the same glass that's in your sight

blocks.title: Drink prices, straight up
blocks.html: Drinks in beach clubs and clubs are usually 2–3x the price of a convenience-store beer. A lot of people start with cheap beers from a shop first, then hit the club later in the night. Cocktails at beach bars start around ฿120–350 depending on the place, and prices climb in high season.

blocks.text: Night 3 — Soi Green Mango, big clubs and live music

blocks.html: Tonight is for serious dancers. Soi Green Mango in Chaweng is the island's big-club street. Green Mango Club has a huge dance floor that holds over a thousand people, with chart music and DJs. Nearby is Soi Reggae, where the two-storey Reggae Pub plays live music with a packed dance floor running late. If you want something more relaxed, head to Lamai Beach, where the bars are smaller, the music is reggae and classic rock, and the crowd is a wider mix of ages.

items: Green Mango Club — the biggest superclub dance floor in Chaweng, chart music, Thai and international DJs. It starts filling up after midnight and is usually at its liveliest around 2am, once Ark Bar closes
Reggae Pub (Soi Reggae) — a two-storey pub with live music and a big dance floor, busy and laid-back, open late
Small beer bars in the soi — pool tables and cheaper drinks than the big clubs, good for warming up before you hit the dance floor
Lamai Beach — more low-key than Chaweng, small bars, live reggae/rock, good if you don't want it too loud

items.activity: Warm up at a small beer bar in the soi, or sit and listen to live music at Reggae Pub
items.note: The dance floors are still empty around now, and drinks are cheaper than the big clubs

items.activity: Head into Green Mango Club as the crowd builds
items.note: Some nights have a cover charge or include a drink, check on the spot. Some entry tickets can be swapped for a drink

items.activity: The floor peaks after Ark Bar closes and the crowd moves over
items.note: Watch your valuables, keep your bag on you, and don't leave your phone on the table
Agree with your friends to leave together. Don't head back alone when you're drunk

blocks.text: Party smart — what to know before you head out

blocks.html: Samui is a great place for a night out, but it's a tourist island and there are things to watch for. We want you to have fun and get home in one piece, so here's the honest rundown.

items: Drink in moderation and watch your own glass — only drink from a glass that's been in your sight, don't accept drinks from strangers, and if you put it down and walk off, just order a fresh one

Get back to your hotel safely — book a ride through an app or always agree on the price before you get on, settle the fare clearly, don't head back alone late at night, and plan to leave with your friends
Riding a motorbike home drunk = don't — many roads on the island are steep and dark, and motorbike accidents on Samui are common. If you've been drinking, call a ride and don't drive yourself
Valuables and passport — carry only what you need, leave your passport at the hotel, and keep your bag on you in crowded spots

Check the weather if you plan to swim at night — some people like getting in the sea after a party, but when the wind and waves pick up or it's raining, stay out of the water, especially while drinking. You can't see the currents in the dark
Set a budget in your head — beach clubs and clubs can have cover charges, minimum spends, and bar-priced drinks. Carry some backup cash and know your card limit

blocks.title: The season changes the vibe
blocks.html: In high season (roughly Dec–Apr), clubs and beach clubs are packed, there are lots of events, and drink and hotel prices climb · during the monsoon (roughly Oct–Nov) it rains often and some beachside events may be cancelled, so always check the venue's page before you go.

blocks.text: Pick the night that fits your style

items.name: With your partner / want to chill
items.blurb: Focus on Night 1 in Bophut, a beach bar watching the fire show, quiet cocktails, no need for a big club to have a good time

items.name: With a group of friends / want to party
items.blurb: Do Night 2 at the Chaweng beach clubs, then carry on to Night 3 on Soi Green Mango and dance until late, and plan to leave together

items.name: On a budget
items.blurb: Start with convenience-store beers, walk the Friday Walking Street in Bophut, then pick just one club night

faq.q: Where should I go out at night on Koh Samui?
faq.a: If you want to chill by the sea and watch a fire show, go to Bophut Fisherman's Village, somewhere like CoCo Tam's · if you want to party on the beach and hit a big club, go to Chaweng, with Ark Bar and Soi Green Mango · while Lamai is more low-key, focused on live reggae and classic rock.

faq.q: How much do drinks cost at Samui beach clubs?
faq.a: Cocktails at beach bars and beach clubs start around ฿120–350 depending on the place, which is about 2–3x the price of a convenience-store beer. That's why a lot of people start drinking at a shop first, then move on to a club. Prices climb in high season.

faq.q: How late do clubs in Chaweng stay open?
faq.a: Ark Bar is open until around 2am, while the big clubs like Green Mango and Reggae Pub on Soi Green Mango/Soi Reggae are usually at their liveliest after midnight and keep going until 4–5am in high season.

faq.q: How do I stay safe on a night out in Samui?
faq.a: Drink in moderation and always watch your own glass, don't accept drinks from strangers, get back to your hotel by booking a ride through an app or agreeing on the price before you get on, don't ride a motorbike while drunk because the island's roads are steep and dark, and plan to leave with your friends rather than heading back alone.

faq.q: Which day is the Bophut Walking Street?
faq.a: Bophut Fisherman's Village closes the street into a Walking Street every Friday evening, roughly 17:00–23:00, with food, live music and craft stalls. It's the liveliest night of the week in the area.
